This article keeps that limit. The 30 months for finished equipment and the half year for the Japanese parts inside it are different measurements of different things. The item-level lead times (16.4 weeks on average, substrate materials 10 to 30 weeks, assembly and packaging equipment 23 to 37 weeks, chemicals and process materials 10 to 17 weeks, 82% seeing higher demand, 42% of materials and 38% of equipment suppliers reporting longer lead times) are News Tomato's reading of the SEMI and McKinsey 2026 semiconductor supply chain survey; what SEMI's own survey page states directly is 200-plus respondents, lead times 27% above historical norms, 88% of suppliers expecting revenue growth over 12 months, and leading-edge capacity at its limit while downstream inventories pile up. The full survey report was not examined. Samsung Electro-Mechanics' 26.0% (CCL and PPG purchase price), 28.1% (package substrate selling price) and 2.4357 trillion won in nine-month package solution sales were read from the published quarterly report, while LG Innotek's 13.7% and the raw material inventory figures (Samsung Electro-Mechanics 66.7bn to 102.2bn won, LG Innotek 34.6bn to 39.6bn won) are as News Tomato cited them from both companies' quarterly reports and were not checked against the originals. Intel's $5.3bn to $6.1bn is the expected outlay for two substrate supply contracts signed after the third quarter closed, of which $3.3bn is due by the end of 2027. Counterpoint's 20% is a forecast for around 2027. The September 2028 start at Sejong and June 2030 at Vietnam follow the JoongAng Ilbo report; News Tomato writes 'gradual mass production from next year', so the timing is reported differently.
